summary: sextant-cli-linux-arm64 ships a WebRTC-tunneled remote PTY agent (backdoor)
details: The npm package ships a ~12 MB linux/arm64 Go ELF binary ('sxt') whose linked packages include the full Pion WebRTC stack (webrtc/v4, ice/v4, dtls/v3, turn/v5, datachannel, sctp, rtp), a WebSocket client (coder/websocket), a QR-code generator (skip2/go-qrcode), and pty symbols. This composition implements the standard shape of a remote-shell agent: a WebSocket/WebRTC transport delivers bytes into an interactive PTY on the installer's host, giving a remote peer arbitrary command execution on that machine. WebRTC signalling plus QR-code pairing is chosen to traverse NAT and evade outbound-firewall inspection. The package's only human-readable identifier in package.json is a license URL pointing to https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control; the account handle and repository name align with the binary's remote-control capability rather than any benign purpose declared by the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
